miss_rate.value: 45/171 = 26.3% (blind re-audit, verified); up to 61/187 = 32.6% if the 16 unsettled candidates are real
miss_rate.note: Second blind audit (two independent auditors, 2026-11-16) against the list after three closure passes: 225 in-definition auditor plants, 126 already in the ledger. Two plant-finders checked all 71 unmatched candidates: 46 new base plants (45 in definition, 18 of them boundary: compact attachments, grinders, mulchers, dredges, mixed-market shops), 10 excluded (out of vertical, offices, dealers, or fabrication contracted out), 15 unverified. Without the 18 boundary misses, 27 core misses remain (27/153 = 17.6%). All 46 are now in the ledger as base records; merging them does not lower the measured rate. Misses cluster in CONEXPO-CON/AGG exhibitors the EPA-registry closure passes never reached. One verified miss ranks inside the top 40 by the profiling key with counted welder postings: General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND, rank 22, two dated postings with a sign-on bonus (site tie inferred under the campus rule); it is not profiled.

known_limits: Partial: the blind re-audit's verified miss rate is 26.3%, over the 20% done threshold. Crusher, screen and asphalt-plant makers look close to complete; small attachment and bucket makers, small conveyor and aggregate fabricators, and Tier 1 weldment shops are not.

One verified miss ranks in the top 40 with counted welder postings and is not profiled: General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND (rank 22; postings dated 2026-06-17 and 2026-09-16, $1,000 sign-on bonus; site tie inferred).

About 155 EPA registry rows and named leads from closure remain unverified, plus 15 re-audit candidates and leads such as Tricon's other plants, Power Curbers' Cedar Falls and McHenry plants, HitchDoc's Kwik-Way Sioux Falls plant and Amerequip's New Holstein plants.
Fact-check: round 1 11.4%; round 2 (all 47 profiles, rotated) 3.3%; round 3 (the 19 newest profiles) 4.2%. All corrections applied. A separate sample of 25 closure base records found 1.5%.

Material scores 0 on 57 of 66 profiled plants: mining and construction sources rarely state a welded part's size or weight, and payloads, bucket capacities and machine classes do not count as part sizes.

Paladin Dexter MI is profiled as a boundary plant: no Paladin page says what it builds, and EPA's facility name (Sweepster-Harley Attachments) points to sweeper and broom attachments, which would exclude it under the M-B New Holstein ruling.
Only 66 of 352 included plants are profiled; base records carry no score.
Auditor B could see file names (not contents) in the shared scratchpad during the re-audit, so its blindness is slightly weaker than auditor A's.
